en.greeting: Hi! Today is about English at real speed: words that melt together, slang from films, people talking over each other and jokes you hear but don't quite get. You'll learn what to listen for, so that the films and podcasts you watch start making sense.

steps.title: Real speed: words that melt
steps.text: You know elision, 'wouldja' and gonna/wanna/gotta from B2, and from C1 that the last version of a self-correction is the fact. Now the speed goes up: groups of words melt into one **reduced form**.
steps.body: **kinda** = kind of · **dunno** = don't know · **lemme** = let me · **gimme** = give me · **whaddya** = what do you · **d'you** = do you · **gotcha** = I understand · very casual US: **Jeet?** = Did you eat? Trap: **I was gonna call you** = I planned to, **but I didn't** (a *but* usually follows). How to listen: catch the stressed words first, then rebuild the small ones. Honest note: our audio is one calm voice at normal speed; real speed comes from the films and podcasts you watch.

pairs.id: kinda = kind of → agak malam nih

steps.title: Listen: a quick reply
steps.text: Catch the strong words first, then rebuild the short forms.

question.listen: Honestly? I dunno. I'm kinda busy this week, but I wanna help if I can. Can we talk about it tomorrow morning?
question.prompt: Rina asks her colleague Sari to help with a client presentation. Listen to Sari's reply. What does Sari mean?
options: She isn't sure yet: she's quite busy, but she'd like to help.
She can't help at all, because she's far too busy.
She'll help today, because she isn't busy this week.
question.explanation: **I dunno** = I don't know (she isn't sure), **kinda busy** = kind of busy (quite busy), **I wanna help** = I want to help. So: not sure yet, but willing. She doesn't say no, and she says she IS busy.

steps.title: Fillers, vague words and film slang
steps.text: Fast speakers also use words that carry little meaning, and slang that depends on the country.
steps.body: **Fillers:** *like, you know, I mean, basically*: let them pass. **Vague words:** *and stuff, or whatever, -ish* (*sevenish* = about seven). **Quotatives:** *he's like, '…'* / *she goes, '…'* = he said / she said. This *like* isn't *suka*: it's Indonesian *terus dia kayak, '…'*. **Slang:** US *I'm down* = I'll join (but *I'm feeling down* = sad), *my bad* = my mistake; UK *gutted* = very disappointed, *knackered* = very tired, *cheers* = thanks. Understand them; don't write them in emails.

pairs.en: We can get snacks or whatever.

steps.title: Slang in a chat
steps.text: Use the context: what kind of message is Jake answering?

question.prompt: Budi messages his American friend Jake: 'Futsal on Saturday night?' Jake replies: 'Yeah, I'm down! What time?' What does Jake mean?
options: He's feeling sad, so he won't come.
He isn't sure yet and will reply later.
He'd like to come and play.
question.explanation: **I'm down** is US slang for *I'm in, I'll join*, and *Yeah* and *What time?* confirm it. *I'm feeling down* would mean sad: the context (an invitation) tells you which one it is.

steps.title: When everyone talks at once
steps.text: Our audio is one voice, so it can't overlap: here you practise with written transcripts. For the real thing, use sitcoms, panel shows and the resources.
steps.body: In real talk people interrupt and stop mid-sentence (**—** in a transcript). **1. Follow the main thread:** what is the group deciding? Note each proposal. **2. Turn-taking cues:** *Sorry, go on / No, you go* = giving the turn; *Can I just… / Hang on* = taking it; *Let me just finish* = keeping it. **3. Back-channelling ≠ agreement:** *mm-hm, yeah, right* = I'm listening (like Indonesian *iya, iya*). **4. The decision** is the last proposal someone accepts: *Let's go with… / OK, Thursday then / Thursday it is*.

pairs.en: Sorry, can I just jump in?
pairs.id: Maaf, boleh aku menyela? → mengambil giliran

pairs.en: Hold on, let me just finish.

pairs.id: Hmm. Iya. Oke. → aku mendengarkan (bukan: setuju)

steps.title: Read: a team call
steps.text: Separate 'I'm listening' from 'I agree'.

question.prompt:
From a team call (— = cut off):
Pak Hasan: So we halve the budget for the Surabaya event and —
Dimas: Mm-hm.
Pak Hasan: — put the rest into online ads.
Dimas: Yeah. Right. Sorry, can I just — halving it? I really don't think that works.
What is Dimas's view of the plan?
options: He agrees: he said 'Yeah' and 'Right'.
He disagrees with halving the budget.
He wants to spend more on online ads.
question.explanation: **Mm-hm, Yeah, Right** while Pak Hasan talks are back-channelling: 'I'm listening'. **Sorry, can I just —** takes the turn, and his real view follows: *I really don't think that works*. He never mentions spending more on ads.

steps.title: Films and series: a subtitles plan
steps.text: Honest truth: this app teaches what to listen for; native speed comes from hours of real shows and podcasts. Here's how to make those hours count.
steps.body: **1. English subtitles first**, not Indonesian: you hear and read the same words, and learn how *gonna* or *whaddya* sounds. **2. Rewatch** a short scene without subtitles. **3. Replay** what you missed: back 10 seconds, guess, check. Knew the words but didn't hear them? It was a reduced form: say the line aloud. **4. Choose shows** with lots of everyday talk and the same characters (sitcoms, workplace dramas) before noisy action films; mix British and American. Subtitles often shorten speech and drop fillers: that's normal.

steps.title: How a joke works
steps.text: You can understand every word and still miss the joke. Here's why, and how a stand-up joke is built.
steps.body: Jokes get lost through **cultural references** (a show, a person, an event you don't know), **wordplay** (one word, two meanings), **timing** (a pause before the punchline: … in text) and **callbacks** (an earlier joke that comes back). A stand-up joke = **setup** (builds an expectation) → **punchline** (breaks it, usually with the **last word**). British humour leans on irony, understatement and deadpan (a straight face); American humour is often more direct and energetic. Tendencies only. All jokes here are original practice texts.

examples.en: My new phone has face recognition. Every morning it looks at me and asks for my password.
examples.id: HP baruku punya pengenal wajah. Tiap pagi dia menatapku lalu minta kata sandi. (punchline: password)

examples.en: The intern asked where the minutes of the meeting were. I said, 'Somewhere between hour one and hour three.'
examples.id: Anak magang bertanya di mana notulen rapatnya. Kujawab, 'Di antara jam pertama dan jam ketiga.' (plesetan: minutes = notulen / menit)

examples.en: For my holiday in Bali, I packed sunscreen, a hat and a laptop full of work.
examples.id: Untuk liburan ke Bali, aku membawa tabir surya, topi dan laptop penuh pekerjaan. (rule of three: hal ketiga mematahkan pola)

steps.title: Find the punchline
steps.text: Look for the word that breaks the expectation the setup built.

question.prompt:
Original practice joke:
'My mum always told me I could become anything I wanted. Well, I'm thirty-five now, and I've finally become… tired.'
Which word is the punchline?
options: anything
thirty-five
tired
question.explanation: The setup (*become anything I wanted*) makes you expect a dream job: a doctor, a pilot. The last word, **tired**, breaks that expectation. The pause (…) before it is the timing. *anything* and *thirty-five* are part of the setup.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip each card. Try to say the meaning before you look.

steps.title: Listen at real speed
steps.text: This is where the real practice happens: a video on reduced forms, a casual British conversation with three friends cutting each other off, and tips for learning from films and series.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini tentang bahasa Inggris dengan kecepatan asli: kata-kata yang melebur, slang dari film, orang yang bicara tumpang tindih, dan lelucon yang terdengar tapi tidak sepenuhnya tertangkap. Kamu akan belajar apa yang perlu didengarkan, supaya film dan podcast yang kamu tonton mulai masuk akal.

steps.title: Kecepatan asli: kata-kata yang melebur
steps.text: Dari B2 kamu kenal bunyi yang hilang, 'wouldja' dan gonna/wanna/gotta, dan dari C1 bahwa versi terakhir dari koreksi diri adalah faktanya. Sekarang kecepatannya naik: beberapa kata melebur jadi satu **bentuk ringkas** (reduced form).
steps.body: **kinda** = kind of (agak) · **dunno** = don't know · **lemme** = let me · **gimme** = give me · **whaddya** = what do you · **d'you** = do you · **gotcha** = aku paham · Amerika yang sangat santai: **Jeet?** = Did you eat? Jebakan: **I was gonna call you** = tadinya mau menelepon, **tapi tidak jadi** (biasanya diikuti *but*). Cara menyimak: tangkap dulu kata yang ditekan, lalu susun kembali kata-kata kecilnya. Catatan jujur: audio kami satu suara tenang dengan kecepatan normal; kecepatan asli datang dari film dan podcast yang kamu tonton.

pairs.id: kinda = kind of → agak malam nih

steps.title: Dengarkan: jawaban singkat
steps.text: Tangkap dulu kata-kata yang kuat, lalu susun kembali bentuk ringkasnya.

question.listen: Honestly? I dunno. I'm kinda busy this week, but I wanna help if I can. Can we talk about it tomorrow morning?
question.prompt: Rina meminta rekan kerjanya, Sari, membantu presentasi untuk klien. Dengarkan jawaban Sari. Apa maksud Sari?
options: She isn't sure yet: she's quite busy, but she'd like to help.
She can't help at all, because she's far too busy.
She'll help today, because she isn't busy this week.
question.explanation: **I dunno** = I don't know (dia belum yakin), **kinda busy** = kind of busy (cukup sibuk), **I wanna help** = I want to help (dia ingin membantu). Jadi: belum pasti, tapi mau. Dia tidak menolak, dan dia bilang dia MEMANG sibuk.

steps.title: Kata pengisi, kata samar dan slang film
steps.text: Penutur yang cepat juga memakai kata-kata yang hampir tidak bermakna, dan slang yang bergantung pada negaranya.
steps.body: **Kata pengisi:** *like, you know, I mean, basically*: biarkan lewat. **Kata samar:** *and stuff* (dan lain-lain), *or whatever* (atau apalah), *-ish* (*sevenish* = sekitar jam tujuh). **Pengantar kutipan:** *he's like, '…'* / *she goes, '…'* = dia bilang. *Like* ini bukan *suka*: sama dengan *terus dia kayak, '…'*. **Slang:** US *I'm down* = aku ikut (tapi *I'm feeling down* = sedih), *my bad* = salahku; UK *gutted* = kecewa berat, *knackered* = capek banget, *cheers* = makasih. Pahami; jangan ditulis di email.

pairs.en: We can get snacks or whatever.

steps.title: Slang di obrolan
steps.text: Pakai konteksnya: pesan seperti apa yang dijawab Jake?

question.prompt: Budi mengirim pesan ke temannya dari Amerika, Jake: 'Futsal on Saturday night?' Jake membalas: 'Yeah, I'm down! What time?' Apa maksud Jake?
options: He's feeling sad, so he won't come.
He isn't sure yet and will reply later.
He'd like to come and play.
question.explanation: **I'm down** adalah slang Amerika untuk *aku ikut*, dan *Yeah* serta *What time?* menegaskannya. *I'm feeling down* baru berarti sedih: konteksnya (sebuah ajakan) memberitahumu yang mana.

steps.title: Saat semua orang bicara bersamaan
steps.text: Audio kami satu suara, jadi tidak bisa tumpang tindih: di sini kamu berlatih dengan transkrip tertulis. Untuk yang sungguhan, pakai sitkom, acara panel dan sumber belajarnya.
steps.body: Dalam obrolan nyata orang saling memotong dan berhenti di tengah kalimat (**—** di transkrip). **1. Ikuti alur utamanya:** apa yang sedang diputuskan kelompok itu? Catat setiap usulan. **2. Penanda giliran:** *Sorry, go on / No, you go* = memberi giliran; *Can I just… / Hang on* = mengambil giliran; *Let me just finish* = menahan giliran. **3. Back-channelling ≠ setuju:** *mm-hm, yeah, right* = aku mendengarkan (seperti *iya, iya*). **4. Keputusannya** adalah usulan terakhir yang diterima seseorang: *Let's go with… / OK, Thursday then / Thursday it is*.

pairs.id: Hmm. Iya. Oke. → aku mendengarkan (bukan: setuju)

steps.title: Baca: rapat tim online
steps.text: Bedakan 'aku mendengarkan' dari 'aku setuju'.

question.prompt:
Dari rapat tim online (— = terpotong):
Pak Hasan: So we halve the budget for the Surabaya event and —
Dimas: Mm-hm.
Pak Hasan: — put the rest into online ads.
Dimas: Yeah. Right. Sorry, can I just — halving it? I really don't think that works.
Bagaimana pendapat Dimas tentang rencana itu?
options: He agrees: he said 'Yeah' and 'Right'.
He disagrees with halving the budget.
He wants to spend more on online ads.
question.explanation: **Mm-hm, Yeah, Right** saat Pak Hasan bicara adalah back-channelling: 'aku mendengarkan'. **Sorry, can I just —** mengambil giliran, lalu pendapat aslinya menyusul: *I really don't think that works* (menurutku itu tidak akan berhasil). Dia sama sekali tidak menyebut tambahan dana iklan.

steps.title: Film dan serial: rencana subtitel
steps.text: Jujur saja: aplikasi ini mengajarkan apa yang perlu didengarkan; kecepatan asli datang dari berjam-jam tontonan dan podcast sungguhan. Begini caranya supaya jam-jam itu berguna.
steps.body: **1. Subtitel bahasa Inggris dulu**, bukan bahasa Indonesia: kamu mendengar dan membaca kata yang sama, dan belajar bunyi *gonna* atau *whaddya*. **2. Tonton ulang** adegan pendek tanpa subtitel. **3. Putar ulang** yang terlewat: mundur 10 detik, tebak, cek. Tahu katanya tapi tidak menangkap bunyinya? Itu bentuk ringkas: ucapkan kalimatnya keras-keras. **4. Pilih tontonan** yang banyak obrolan sehari-hari dan tokohnya tetap (sitkom, drama kantor) sebelum film laga yang bising; campur British dan Amerika. Subtitel sering memendekkan ucapan dan membuang kata pengisi: itu normal.

steps.title: Cara kerja lelucon
steps.text: Kamu bisa paham setiap kata tapi tetap tidak menangkap leluconnya. Ini sebabnya, dan cara lelucon stand-up dibangun.
steps.body: Lelucon sering tidak tertangkap karena **rujukan budaya** (acara, tokoh, peristiwa yang tidak kamu kenal), **permainan kata** (satu kata, dua makna), **timing** (jeda sebelum punchline: … di teks) dan **callback** (lelucon sebelumnya yang muncul lagi). Lelucon stand-up = **setup** (pengantar yang membangun harapan) → **punchline** (pamungkas yang mematahkannya, biasanya **kata terakhir**). Humor British cenderung ironi, understatement dan deadpan (wajah datar); humor Amerika sering lebih langsung dan bersemangat. Hanya kecenderungan. Semua lelucon di sini teks latihan orisinal.

steps.title: Temukan punchline-nya
steps.text: Cari kata yang mematahkan harapan yang dibangun setup-nya.

question.prompt:
Lelucon latihan orisinal:
'My mum always told me I could become anything I wanted. Well, I'm thirty-five now, and I've finally become… tired.'
Kata mana yang menjadi punchline?
options: anything
thirty-five
tired
question.explanation: Setup-nya (*become anything I wanted*) membuatmu menduga pekerjaan impian: dokter, pilot. Kata terakhir, **tired** (capek), mematahkan dugaan itu. Jeda (…) sebelumnya adalah timing-nya. *anything* dan *thirty-five* bagian dari setup.
